name: MCPJam Inspector MCPJam-fault error (prod)
aplQuery: | summarize Count = count() by tostring(slug), tostring(route), tostring(source)
description: WARN (bake) — owner: marcelo. A failure the classifier attributed to MCPJam ITSELF occurred in prod. Zero tolerance: any single occurrence fires.

THIS IS THE MONITOR THE WHOLE PROGRAM EXISTS FOR. Every other monitor here measures volume or novelty and cannot tell our outage from a user's server dying. This one fires only on `origin == 'mcpjam'` — the effective origin from the capture decision, after boundary promotion, not the catalog's declared value.

WHY WARN AND NOT PAGE: the plan gates M2 on a seven-day bake of the corrected effective-origin path, which starts at the deploy that carries #4018/#4025/#4029. Tier is the only thing held back — the alert still posts to #mcpjam-alerts, and PAGE/WARN treatment is currently identical anyway (see README 'PAGE vs WARN notifiers'). To promote after a clean bake, change `tier` to PAGE and `notifier` to mcpjam-alerts-page, then re-apply. Do NOT promote by raising the threshold above 0 — zero tolerance is the design.

MEASURED BEFORE ENABLING (2026-08-15, prod, 7d): ZERO rows match. Origin coverage on `http.request.failed` began 2026-08-11 and now runs ~91% (08-12 443/505, 08-13 212/237, 08-14 152/167); the large unattributed bucket before 08-11 predates the field and is not a coverage hole. So a first-run burst is not expected — but see the KNOWN BLIND SPOT below before reading silence as health.

KNOWN BLIND SPOT — READ BEFORE TRUSTING SILENCE. Two routes still emit 5xx with NO origin at all, so they cannot reach this monitor no matter how badly they fail. Measured over 72h to 2026-08-15: `/api/v1/projects/:projectId/eval-ingest/report` internal_error 500 (44) and `/api/web/oauth/metadata` internal_error 500/502 (55). Both are MCPJam's own routes answering 500, i.e. exactly this monitor's target class. Closing them is the first bake action, not a follow-up. Track with: ['inspector-logs'] | where _time > ago(24h) | where event == 'http.request.failed' | where tostring(environment) in ('prod','production') | summarize total = count(), unattributed = countif(isempty(tostring(origin))) by tostring(route) | where unattributed > 0 | sort by unattributed desc

ALSO KNOWN: `release` is empty on 100% of prod rows (0 of 2129 over 7d) despite #3982's resolveRelease(). Every 'compare release across the deploy boundary' triage step in this directory is currently dead — including step 3 below. Establish the failing build from deploy timing until that is fixed.

SCOPE: `event in (...)`, never `level ==` — typed events carry no `level`. `route.operation.failed` is included because chat answers over a 200 SSE stream and the JSON-RPC bridge answers over HTTP 200, so those failures never reach `http.request.failed` at all; it lands with the deploy of #4025/#4029 and will read zero until then. `chat.session.persist.failed` is deliberately NOT matched: it also has a field called `origin`, but it carries a product surface (ChatOrigin), not an ErrorOrigin, and joining the two axes would produce nonsense.

THE ALERT MAY CARRY ONLY A COUNT. Grouped-column rendering in Slack is unverified (see README 'Verifying delivery'), so do not depend on slug/route/source appearing in the message. NAME THE FAILURE: ['inspector-logs'] | where _time > ago(2h) | where event in ('http.request.failed','route.operation.failed') | where tostring(origin) == 'mcpjam' | where tostring(environment) in ('prod','production') | summarize n = count(), orgs = dcount(orgId), firstSeen = min(_time), lastSeen = max(_time) by tostring(slug), tostring(route), tostring(source), tostring(errorCode) | sort by n desc

1. Trust it more than the other monitors. A row here is not a volume heuristic — a classifier looked at the failure and concluded it was ours. The false-positive mode is a MISCLASSIFICATION, so if you disagree with the verdict, fix the rule that produced it (the slug's catalog origin, or the hop declared at `source`) rather than filtering it out here.

2. Read `source` first when present. It is the exact catch-site id: `mcp.chat-v2.backend-stream` (our Convex /stream answered badly), `mcp.bridge.rpc` (a user's server rejected a message WE built), `mcp.chat-v2.agentic-loop`, `chat.harness-turn`. `slug` tells you the class; `source` tells you the code path.
3. Check the deploy boundary. `release` is unpopulated today (see above), so correlate `firstSeen` against deploy times by hand until that is fixed.
4. Check breadth. `orgs` above 1 on a fresh slug means it is systematic and not one customer's edge case.

5. Cross-check Sentry. Capture policy is `origin == 'mcpjam'` and nothing else, so every row here SHOULD have a matching Sentry event with tags `error_origin`, `error_slug`, `capture_source`, and (when a boundary drove it) `error_boundary`. A row here with no Sentry event means the capture half regressed and is its own bug.

ROLLBACK: revert the definition file, then run `node ops/axiom-monitors/apply.mjs --apply --only inspector-mcpjam-fault`. The --apply flag is required: the script defaults to read-only plan mode. To remove entirely: `node ops/axiom-monitors/apply.mjs --delete inspector-mcpjam-fault`.
